sentences.text: The front base of its crest showed a flat-topped margin, a contrast to the grooved crest bases seen in related forms.
A small, blunt protrusion at the crest base is unique among its close relatives.
The sole specimen was uncovered in 2014 by Will Thurbin at Sudmour Point on the Isle of Wight’s southwest coast.
It was donated to the Dinosaur Isle museum and catalogued as IWCMS 2014.82.
Pêgas and Holgado reassessed the material in a 2026 publication.
The generic name combines Greek terms meaning “callused” and “beak” to refer to a callus-like palate projection.
Tylodorhynchus is placed in the coloborhynchine subgroup of the anhanguerid pterosaurs.
The genus was formally named by Pêgas and Holgado in 2026.
It was erected for the species previously assigned to Uktenadactylus rodriguesae because it differs from Uktenadactylus wadleighi, which aligns more closely with Nicorhynchus.
Tylodorhynchus lived during the Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous.
Some researchers propose that the bulbous projection observed in Uktenadactylus wadleighi may represent a pathological condition rather than a normal anatomical trait.
Earlier evaluations argued that minor differences from Coloborhynchus clavirostris were insufficient to justify a separate species designation.
